topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series by outlining the multidisciplinary audience, course structure, and specific learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine cancer fundamentally as a disruption of normal differentiation programs, tissue architecture, and cellular regulation through accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the diagnostic and histological distinction between benign and malignant tumors, focusing on basement membrane invasion, metastatic pathways, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the standard conventions and exceptions used to name and categorize benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical and systemic mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors impair physiological function and lead to death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the prevalence of different neoplasms in human populations and across diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles, methods, and efficacy of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the clinical rationale for early tumor detection and compare screening modalities across various cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing remarks by revisiting the core learning outcomes and looking ahead to practical sessions.
